subject: Incubator cohort — eligibility for startup + nonprofit blended credits
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@brightroots.org>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Liu <jason@seedspring.vc>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: volume credits & nonprofit eligibility for our cohort

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the intro at the conference last week. BrightRoots runs a six-month incubator that supports both early-stage startups and a small cohort of registered 501(c)(3) nonprofits. We wire a small stipend for each org and provide product credits.

Two quick questions about Redwood's hosted API pricing: can we get a single credit allocation that covers both types of orgs, and is there a standard path to apply nonprofit eligibility (we can provide IRS docs)? We're trying to determine whether to include Redwood as a preferred credits partner for the next cohort (launching July 6).

Ideal outcome for us: a baseline rate that's discounted for cohort participants, plus a small per-participant credit pool (~$2k total) we can distribute. If there's an incubator/partner program or an existing non-profit verification workflow, please point me to it.

Appreciate any guidance —
Elena
Program Director, BrightRoots Incubator
incubator@brightroots.org
From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightroots.org>
Cc: Jason Liu <jason@seedspring.vc>, mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: volume credits & nonprofit eligibility for our cohort

Hi Elena —

Great to hear from you and congrats on the upcoming cohort. Short answers up front: yes, we can do a blended approach (startup + nonprofit) and we have an existing nonprofit verification flow. A few notes so I set expectations correctly:

- Baseline hosted API pricing is usage-based; discounts for partners are typically delivered via a combination of credits (one-off or recurring) and a temporary per-token discount applied to the partner account.
- For nonprofits, we require documentation (EIN + 501(c)(3) letter) to qualify for the nonprofit rate. We also support partner-managed credit pools.

To proceed I need:
1) A short list of expected cohort size and an estimate of monthly tokens per participant (ballpark is fine).
2) Scanned nonprofit docs for the orgs that claim nonprofit status (we can fast-track verification).
3) Confirmation whether BrightRoots wants Redwood to manage the credit distribution (we can issue cohort codes) or if you prefer per-organization subaccounts.

I've looped in Mateo (partnerships) to scope a partner offer. If you want a formal proposal we can turn around an incubator program letter with suggested credit amounts and a blended rate for the cohort.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Partnerships | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
From: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: draft offer calc for BrightRoots cohort

Soojin —

Draft thinking below for the incubator program:

- Cohort size: 12 orgs (estimate from Elena). Assume 3 nonprofits + 9 startups.
- Suggested credit pool: $2,000 total credits (USD) applied as cohort promo codes (splitable).
- Blended baseline discount: 20% off standard hosted API per-token rate for first 6 months for all cohort participants. Nonprofits that pass verification get an additional 15% nonprofit adjustment (stackable).
- Eligibility: nonprofits must submit EIN + 501(c)(3) letter; startups qualify if they are part of BrightRoots official roster (we will verify).

Notes/risks:
- If any single org uses >50% of the credit pool, we should set guardrails or transition them to a standard committed pricing path.
- Need legal approval on stacking discounts (promo + nonprofit). Also need to confirm billing flow if BrightRoots wants to manage the funds vs. Redwood issuing codes.

Recommend we present a short memorandum to Elena with two options: (A) Redwood-managed promo codes + verification flow, (B) per-org subaccounts with a managed discount and optional reserved capacity add-on.

-Mateo
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightroots.org>
Cc: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2026 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: BrightRoots cohort offer (summary)

Elena —

Thanks for the details. Attached is a short proposal (incubator-MAP-v2.pdf) summarizing 2 options:

Option A (simpler):
- Redwood issues a $2,000 cohort credit pool as promo codes you distribute.
- 20% off hosted API per-token rate for six months for all cohort participants.
- Nonprofits that supply 501(c)(3) docs get an extra 15% nonprofit adjustment (applied after the 20%).
- Guardrails: single-org usage cap of $800 from the pool; excess usage billed at standard discounted rate.

Option B (managed accounts):
- Per-org subaccounts, cohort discount of 25% for six months (higher because of subaccount work), and Redwood handles nonprofit verification; credits allocated per participant on request.
- Requires a small onboarding fee and an SOW if you want monthly usage reporting integrated into your organizer dashboard.

Next steps: Elena, if you can confirm cohort headcount and whether you want promo-code distribution vs subaccounts, we'll finalize and generate DocuSign links. Also please upload nonprofit docs for the three orgs you expect to designate as nonprofits — I've attached a sample proof template (nonprofit-proof.pdf).

Cheers,
Soojin
From: Elena Morales <elena@brightroots.org>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Liu <jason@seedspring.vc>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: BrightRoots cohort offer (summary)

Soojin / Mateo —

This looks great and fast, thank you. We prefer Option A to keep logistics simple. Confirming estimated cohort size 14 (4 nonprofits, 10 startups). We'll upload the nonprofit docs by Monday. Two quick clarifying points before we sign: 1) can the nonprofit adjustment stack with the 20% promo? (you said yes, but want it in writing), and 2) is the $800 single-org cap per cohort or per month?

If those are both in writing we'll move forward and I can route the DocuSign to our finance contact next week.

Warmly,
Elena
Program Director, BrightRoots Incubator
incubator@brightroots.org
